Click {restore} any time to bring an item back; click the trash icon to destroy it permanently. Items stay in Trash indefinitely until you choose to empty it.

trash.keptHint: Items are kept until you permanently delete them. Restoring puts a chapter back in its original Part when possible (falling back to the last Part if the original has been removed).

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: {settings} is divided into sections — {project} (metadata, goals, statuses, deadlines), {appearance} (themes, fonts, colours, density), {general} (data location & connection), and {backups} (autosave, full backup / restore, and workspace reset). AI providers, routing, usage, and writing-AI settings live in the {ai} menu. Nothing here touches your manuscript prose.

language.label: Language
language.hint: User-interface language. Date and number formatting follow the same locale.

server.headlessHint: Run the server on its own and open the app in any browser — no desktop install needed. The server hosts the UI at:
server.authHint: Off by default. Add a token to require an Authorization: Bearer header on every /v1 API call — for when you run the server exposed beyond this machine.
server.requireLoopback: Require a token even on localhost
server.noTokens: No tokens — the API is open (fine for local-only use).

project.editsUndoHint: Edits flow through the same undo/redo history as your manuscript — ⌘Z restores the previous value.
project.fieldPremisePlaceholder: One- or two-sentence pitch. Used on the Home dashboard and exports.

goals.dailyTargetHint: words/day — drives the Home streak ring

appearance.functionalColoursHint: Success, danger and info — used by status chips, banners and the buttons and tags below. Like the accent, you pick a hue and every shade stays legible in light & dark.
appearance.buttonIntentsHint: Each button has a single {intent} that encodes both colour and visual style. {primary} (solid accent) is the main affordance. {secondary} is outlined neutral for supporting actions. {ghost} is quiet text-only for utility. {functional} follow the functional colours above, {accent2} follows your second accent — all solid fills for clear status. Re-tinting any colour above re-skins them all.
appearance.backgroundsHint: Tint each area independently — every option is tuned to stay legible. Pick a curated swatch or click {custom} for any colour. The {text} row picks the text-colour family used across the app.
appearance.inlinePaperLabel: Apply editor paper to inline fields
appearance.inlinePaperHint: Character, note & worldbuilding rich-text fields pick up the paper tint instead of the surface.
appearance.editorLayoutHint: How the manuscript editor presents your prose while you write.
appearance.editorLayoutPageHint: Centered sheet with margins and running head.
appearance.editorLayoutOverrideNote: Per-document overrides for any of these live in the editor's ⚙ Writing settings — pick {theme} there to fall back to the theme default.
appearance.editorWritingHint: Defaults for the manuscript prose — font size, line spacing, paragraph spacing, and first-line indent. Per-document choices in the editor's ⚙ Writing settings override these.
appearance.buttonStylingHint: Shape, padding, and label casing for every button across the app.
appearance.resetTooltip: Reset every appearance setting to the default look
appearance.presetsHint: Start from a curated look, then fine-tune anything below.
appearance.savePresetCurrentHint: Keep this mix as a preset
appearance.deletePresetMessage: Removes this custom preset. Your current appearance stays as it is.
appearance.resetMessage: Returns every appearance setting — including light/dark mode — to the default look. Your saved custom presets are kept.
appearance.previewProse1: She pressed her thumb to the vellum where the coastline should have been, and felt only the cold weave of the cloth.
appearance.previewProse2: Above her, the deck complained in its joints — and the fog, she now understood, was not weather.
appearance.themeDarkHint: Deep slate surfaces for night writing.
appearance.typographyHint: Choose the typeface for each part of the app, scale the overall size, and tune the sidebar's heading + menu styles.
appearance.displayFontHint: Page titles, big numbers, serif headings.
appearance.editorBodyFontHint: Manuscript prose. Per-document choice can override this in the editor's ⚙ Writing settings.
appearance.uiScaleHint: Scales every label, control, and the prose together.
appearance.sectionHeadingHint: The small labels that group the sidebar nav (e.g. {manuscript}, {storyWorld}).
appearance.menuItemHint: Each sidebar entry — {home}, {chapters}, {characters}, and so on.
appearance.accentsHint: Accent drives selection, the active nav item, buttons and links. Accent 2 is the secondary — rings, rules, peak markers, and the {accent2Intent} intent on buttons and tags.

backups.deleteSelectedMessage: The selected on-disk autosave files are permanently removed. This can't be undone.
backups.deleteAllMessage: Every on-disk autosave file is permanently removed. This can't be undone.
backups.restoreMessage: Saved at {when}. Your current workspace will be overwritten — every project, chapter body, and AI provider. Export a backup first if you want to keep what you have.
backups.autosavePending: Pending — will fire within 10s of the next edit.
backups.autosaveHint: Every edit is also mirrored to a JSON file on disk within ~10s. Two prior generations are kept ({prev} / {prev2}) so a bad write or accidental reset can be recovered without a manual export. Each file is a full workspace bundle — project, AI providers, sessions — so restoring one file brings everything back. By default it lives inside your data folder (shown below); anything OneDrive / Time Machine / your backup tool watches in this folder will pick it up automatically.
backups.emptyList: No autosaves on disk yet. They start appearing after the first edit.
backups.dataFolderHint: Everything JustWrite saves lives here — your books, images, the AI engine and models, and logs — and the autosave folder above sits inside it by default. Move it from {link}.
backups.thisBookHint: {export} the current book as a single {zip} — its text, structure, and images — to move it to another computer or share it, then {import} a {zip2} back as a new book. Each chooser remembers where you last saved.

about.tagline: A local-first writing studio for novels — chapters, cast, and world, all stored on your machine.

providerForm.fieldApiKeyPlaceholder: Optional — leave blank for local providers

Pick Ollama only for an Ollama daemon — its native /api/chat is the only path that honors think:false.
providerForm.runnerOpenai: OpenAI-compatible (most providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM…)
providerForm.runnerOllama: Ollama native (only for an Ollama daemon — honors think:false)
providerForm.tooltipFetchModels: Query GET /v1/models on the Base URL above
providerForm.fieldTierTitle: Attribution pipeline capability bucket for this model. Auto-picked by name pattern; you can pin a different choice if you know better. Guided = scaffolded examples for sub-12B models. Direct = strict rules for 12B-class non-reasoning. Reasoned = strict rules + implicit reasoning for hybrid models (Qwen3:14B+).
providerForm.fieldEmbeddingModelTitle: Optional embedding model — fills the RAG (manuscript chat) index. Leave blank if this provider isn't your embedding provider. OpenAI: text-embedding-3-small. Ollama: nomic-embed-text. Anthropic / Google / OpenRouter generally don't expose embedding endpoints — leave blank.

index.intro: {chapters} is the writing surface — the editor itself. {edit} is where you write, showing a chapter's scenes as a {listView} or {cardView}; {outline} lays out every part, chapter and scene in order; {read} is a clean pass over the whole manuscript. Type {at} to mention any Story Bible entity; the {ai} button in the scene strip opens rewrite, continue and line-edit actions; the {links} panel ties each scene to its characters, location and strands.

ai.triggerTooltip: AI writing assist — Rewrite, Expand, Tighten, Continue, Line edits
ai.unstuckNeedsProse: Write a few lines first — Unstuck needs prose to brainstorm from.
ai.highlightSubjectFirst: Highlight a subject first (a place, object, or moment).
ai.rewriteDesc: Rewrite the passage to be more vivid and specific while preserving meaning, tense, and voice. Selection-only because a whole-scene rewrite is too transformative for one click.
ai.expandDesc: Add sensory detail, interiority, and small actions. Roughly doubles the length without changing voice or tense.
ai.describeDesc: Treat the highlighted text as a subject — a place, person, object, or moment — and add 1–2 paragraphs of fresh sensory prose ABOUT it right after. Additive, not a rewrite; the original passage stays untouched.
ai.sensoryDesc: Sibling to Describe. Instead of streamed prose, get a structured pack of short sensory phrases (smell, sound, touch, temperature, taste, movement, social, period detail). Pick the ones that fit and click to drop them into your manuscript.
ai.tightenDesc: Remove filler words, hedges, and redundant phrases. Keeps the meaning, voice, and tense intact — the result is noticeably shorter. Runs on the selection, or the whole scene if nothing is selected.
ai.continueDesc: Write 2–4 more paragraphs from where the cursor is, matching the voice, tense, and POV of what came before.
ai.guidedDesc: Same as Continue, but you give it a one-line instruction first ("Elena confronts Marcus but he deflects with charm"). The next 2–4 paragraphs honour your direction while matching the voice, tense, and POV of what came before.
ai.unstuckDesc: When you're not sure what should happen next, ask the model for five distinct moves (goal shift, interrupt, setting change, reveal, time cut). Pick one and JustWrite drafts the next 2–4 paragraphs in that direction.
ai.lineEditsHint: Selection, or whole scene if none
ai.clearStrikesDesc: Remove every struck-through original left behind by accepted AI changes (and the originals of still-pending ones — that accepts them). The new text stays.

dialogs.guidedMessage: What should happen next? One sentence is enough — JustWrite will draft the next 2–4 paragraphs in that direction.

identity.title: Identity & core engine
identity.hint: The engine — fill this before anything else.

arc.title: Arc
arc.hint: Frame it as evidence for and against the lie.

voice.title: Voice & presence
voice.hint: How they sound and move — the calibration set.

function.title: Function in the story
function.hint: What they're FOR in the cast.

capabilities.title: Capabilities & limits
capabilities.hint: Genre module — skip for realist fiction.

depth.title: Backstory & depth
depth.hint: Fill only what will surface on the page.

classOrigin.label: Class origin → now
classOrigin.hint: Where they started vs. where they are — the gap is characterization. e.g. dockworker's kid → guild master.

education.label: Education
education.hint: Formal or otherwise — it sets vocabulary and what they notice. e.g. street-taught; convent schooling; self-read.

want.label: Wants
want.hint: e.g. win the guild seat; get her sister out of debt

need.label: Needs
need.hint: e.g. to forgive himself; to stop performing for everyone

lie.label: Lie they believe
lie.hint: e.g. “love has to be earned”; “fear gets you killed”

truth.label: Truth they meet
truth.hint: e.g. “they stayed anyway”; “needing people isn't weakness”

fear.label: Core fear
fear.hint: What they organize their life to avoid — the lie's shadow. e.g. being exposed as a fraud; being left again.

lieOrigin.label: Where the lie began
lieOrigin.hint: Write it as a scene: where, who said what, what they decided. e.g. the night her father called her gift a curse.

contradiction.label: Central contradiction
contradiction.hint: Two things both true about them that don't fit. e.g. brutally honest with strangers, lies to those she loves.

values.label: Values under pressure
values.hint: Three values, ranked — the higher wins until the crisis tests it. e.g. loyalty > truth > safety.

heuristic.label: Decision heuristic
heuristic.hint: One line: “under pressure, they choose ___ over ___.” e.g. protects the crew over the mission.

stakes.label: Stakes
stakes.hint: What breaks — for them and others — if they fail. e.g. the harbor floods; his daughter loses her name.

start.label: Beginning
start.hint: e.g. hiding the gift, keeping her head down

midpoint.label: Midpoint
midpoint.hint: e.g. forced to use it in the open

end.label: End
end.hint: e.g. leads openly — or doubles down and loses them

accent.label: Accent
accent.hint: e.g. soft Southern drawl; clipped city vowels; none

vocabulary.label: Vocabulary
vocabulary.hint: words they favor. e.g. nautical slang; courtroom Latin

tic.label: Speech tic
tic.hint: a verbal habit. e.g. starts sentences with “Look,”

sample.label: Sample line — calm
sample.hint: an ordinary line, in their voice. e.g. “Chart it or lose it.”

register.label: Register
register.hint: Formal ↔ casual — where they sit, and when they slip. e.g. courtly in public, gutter-blunt alone.

rhythm.label: Rhythm
rhythm.hint: Clipped or flowing; do they interrupt or trail off? e.g. short sentences, always interrupting.

forbidden.label: Forbidden words
forbidden.hint: Words this character would never say. e.g. never “sorry”, never “please”.

subtext.label: Subtext habit
subtext.hint: How they avoid saying the real thing. e.g. answers a hard question with a joke.

humor.label: Humor style
humor.hint: Dry / absent / cruel / self-deprecating — “none” is a choice too. e.g. deadpan, never laughs at his own.

languages.label: Languages
languages.hint: What they speak or read — who can they understand that others can't? e.g. reads Old Parian; speaks the trade cant.

sampleAngry.label: Sample line — angry
sampleAngry.hint: An actual furious line they'd say. e.g. “You had one job. One.”

sampleLying.label: Sample line — lying
sampleLying.hint: A line they say while covering or deflecting. e.g. “I was never near the place.”

physicality.label: How they occupy space
physicality.hint: Posture, gait, stillness or motion — one line a scene can borrow. e.g. still and watchful; takes up no space.

presentation.label: Presentation
presentation.hint: What their appearance choices signal — the message, not the looks. e.g. an expensive coat kept deliberately shabby.

stressTells.label: Baseline & stress tells
stressTells.hint: Their normal state, and how fear or lying leaks through. e.g. over-precise hands; goes very quiet.

theme.label: Thematic argument
theme.hint: The side of the story's central question they embody. e.g. lives out “mercy is weakness” — and is proven wrong.

protagonistRelation.label: Relation to protagonist
protagonistRelation.hint: Opposition / mirror / temptation / ally / measuring stick. e.g. mirror — same wound, opposite choice.

selfImage.label: Self-image
selfImage.hint: Who they believe they are. e.g. “a realist” (really a coward).

persona.label: Public persona
persona.hint: Who they perform being. e.g. the unflappable captain.

privateTruth.label: Private truth
privateTruth.hint: Who they actually are — the gaps between these three are engines. e.g. terrified he's becoming his father.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.hint: What reliably provokes them — levers other characters can pull. e.g. mention his brother; call her naive.

allegiances.label: Allegiances & obligations
allegiances.hint: Groups they belong to — and what membership demands. e.g. sworn to the Order; owes a smuggler a life.

escalation.label: How they escalate
escalation.hint: Aggression, withdrawal, sabotage, going over heads… e.g. goes cold and starts quietly planning.

cornered.label: Cornered behavior
cornered.hint: What they do with no good options — who they really are. e.g. burns it down rather than kneel.

abilities.label: Abilities
abilities.hint: Magic, tech, training — what can they actually do? e.g. reads emotions; deadly with a thrown knife.

costs.label: Costs
costs.hint: What each use takes — energy, sanity, time, moral weight. e.g. every casting costs a day of her life.

limits.label: Hard limits
limits.hint: What they can never do — limits make more plot than powers. e.g. can't lie while touching cold iron.

conditions.label: Conditions
conditions.hint: What the ability requires — tools, materials, states. e.g. needs moonlight; needs the true name.

whoKnows.label: Who knows
whoKnows.hint: Who is aware of these capabilities. e.g. only her old mentor knows.

physicalConstants.label: Physical constants
physicalConstants.hint: Only features that appear on the page. e.g. burn scar on the left hand; limps in the cold.

health.label: Conditions & disabilities
health.hint: Anything that changes what's possible in a scene. e.g. deaf in one ear; needs the tonic daily.

timelineAnchors.label: Timeline anchors
timelineAnchors.hint: Birth year + dated events — do the math once. e.g. born 1147; the fire was year 12.

knows.label: Knows at story start
knows.hint: What they already know as the story opens. e.g. knows the king is dead; knows who the traitor is.

doesntKnow.label: Doesn't know
doesntKnow.hint: What they don't know yet — and might act against. e.g. doesn't know she's being followed.

believesWrongly.label: Believes wrongly
believesWrongly.hint: The top source of continuity errors and POV leaks. e.g. believes her brother is still alive.

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.hint: One per line: the secret — who else knows — the reveal. e.g. “killed the steward — only Mira suspects”.

possessions.label: Possessions with story weight
possessions.hint: Objects that will matter — and where each one is. e.g. the dead brother's watch (in her coat).

regrets.label: Regrets
regrets.hint: Compressed backstory plus motivation in one line. e.g. the letter he never sent.

family.label: Family / upbringing
family.hint: Who raised them and what it cost. e.g. estranged from a father who runs the guild.

skills.label: Skills & ceiling
skills.hint: Competence AND its ceiling, so solutions stay fair. e.g. brilliant tactician, hopeless liar.

routines.label: Routines & habits
routines.hint: Useful mainly for disruption when broken. e.g. tea at dawn, always the same cracked cup.

appearance.label: Appearance beyond the constants
appearance.hint: The changeable look, beyond the fixed constants. e.g. tall, ink-stained fingers, never quite still.

tastes.label: Tastes & quirks
tastes.hint: Small preferences that make them a person. e.g. hates music; collects old maps.

analysis.intro: {analysis} is a dashboard of objective data about your manuscript — how much you've written, how fast, how the chapters are structured, and what your prose patterns look like. Almost everything is calculated locally from the text; the only AI surfaces are the {tension} bulk-analyse button and the per-chapter {explain} button under Voice drift.

welcome.tagline: Everything a novel needs — the writing, the world, the plan — in one quiet place.

chapters.title: Chapters & scenes
chapters.body: Draft in a calm, focused editor and shape the manuscript chapter by chapter.

bible.title: Story bible
bible.body: Characters, locations, objects and worldbuilding — every detail linked back to your prose.

plot.title: Plot & strands
plot.body: Follow arcs, beats and subplots as strands running through the whole book.

timeline.title: Timeline & events
timeline.body: Lay out what happens when, and keep your chronology straight.

ai.title: AI assistance
ai.body: Critique, chat with your book and deep analysis — running locally or online, your choice.

goals.title: Goals & pace
goals.body: Set word-count goals, log writing sessions and watch your momentum build.

search.title: Search & replace
search.body: Find anything across the manuscript, and rename or fix it in one sweep.

notes.title: Notes & brainstorm
notes.body: Capture ideas, research and loose threads without leaving your project.

export.title: Export
export.body: Produce PDF, DOCX and EPUB — a clean manuscript ready to send.

aiSetup.title: Set up AI features
aiSetup.body: JustWrite's AI runs where you choose — on this PC, private and free, or through an online provider. You can set this up anytime from the AI page.
aiSetup.quickSetupSub: Local — uses this PC, private & free
